references.phrase: inverse limit of the quotient rings
references.context: Commutative algebra: inverse limit of the projective system of commutative quotient rings R/I^n with compatible quotient maps, consisting of tuples (r_n) satisfying r_{n+1} mod I^n=r_n and componentwise ring operations.
references.reason: The ring-valued inverse-limit construction is reusable and not supplied by the indexed module-only inverse limit.
references.matching_note: Keep ring versus module inverse-limit context; same underlying compatible-tuple pattern but different operations.

references.context: Commutative algebra: quotient ring A/I of a commutative unital ring A by an ideal I, with elements additive cosets a+I, operations induced from A and canonical surjective unital quotient map A→A/I. This includes prime-ideal quotients, polynomial-ring quotients and ideal-power quotients; a quotient's being a field, local ring or R-algebra requires additional conditions.
references.matching_note: This is the ordinary quotient ring by an ideal. Distinct specific features of this occurrence (prime ideal, polynomial base ring, local ring, square-zero ideal or powers) remain in its mathematical source. It is not a general quotient module or a quotient topology.

references.phrase: transition maps given by reduction modulo smaller powers
references.context: Commutative algebra: natural unital quotient ring homomorphisms R/I^{n+1}→R/I^n induced by ideal inclusion I^{n+1}⊆I^n, compatible under composition.
references.reason: The inverse system requires specific well-defined transition homomorphisms, not an arbitrary family of functions.
references.matching_note: Compare globally with canonical quotient ring maps while preserving ideal-power index direction.

references.disposition: The indexing set of positive natural numbers is standard ambient notation.

references.context: Commutative algebra: canonical unital comparison map R→lim_n R/m^n, r↦(r+m^n)_n into the m-adic completion of local ring (R,m).
references.reason: This particular comparison map is a reusable construction tested for being an isomorphism in the completeness definition.
references.matching_note: May be specialized form of the general I-adic completion comparison map; audit candidate equivalence later.

references.context: Ring theory: unital ring isomorphism, a bijective unital ring homomorphism whose inverse also preserves addition, multiplication and identity; here the canonical completion comparison map.
references.reason: The statement that a particular ring homomorphism is an isomorphism presupposes a structured invertibility notion.
references.matching_note: Do not equate with module-only isomorphisms or merely bijections of sets.

references.disposition: Restatement of surjectivity and injectivity of the canonical comparison map, not a new separate completion procedure.

references.context: Commutative algebra: finite polynomial-algebra presentation of an R-algebra S by a quotient R[x_1,…,x_n]/(f_1,…,f_m), with an R-algebra isomorphism to S.
references.reason: The general quotient-ring and R-algebra-isomorphism constructions are prerequisites to describing a finite presentation.

references.reason: A defining ideal generated by polynomial relations is a reusable algebraic construction.

references.context: Commutative algebra: polynomial algebra R[X_i : i in I] over a commutative unital coefficient ring R, for an arbitrary set I of independent indeterminates; each polynomial has finite monomial support. Includes the one-variable and finite-variable cases and polynomial algebras over fields and quotient coefficient rings.
references.matching_note: Reviewed original source's polynomial expression with the common multivariate-polynomial construction. Index-set size and base coefficient ring specialize the same general commutative unital polynomial algebra; do not conflate it with localization, polynomial evaluation, the polynomial quotient or degree.

An ideal of a commutative unital ring is an R-submodule of its regular module R. Finite ideal generation by listed elements is precisely finite generation of that R-module, without asserting finite presentation, principality or a noncommutative two-sided ideal condition.

references.context: Commutative algebra: quotient of a finite-variable polynomial algebra over R by the ideal generated by the given finite polynomial relations, yielding a commutative unital R-algebra.
references.reason: The quotient ring construction is presupposed by the presentation criterion.
references.matching_note: Compare with general ring-quotient missing candidate rather than imposing special ideal properties.

references.phrase: R-algebra isomorphism from the quotient to S
references.context: Commutative algebra: isomorphism of unital R-algebras preserving both ring operations and the specified structure maps from R; not merely an abstract ring or R-module isomorphism.
references.reason: The definition needs an R-algebra-compatible isomorphism, not an arbitrary additive-group bijection.
references.matching_note: Compare later to categorical isomorphism and ring isomorphism with structure-map scope.

references.disposition: Both generators and defining equations must be finite; a finitely generated R-algebra need not be finitely presented over an arbitrary R.

references.phrase: monic polynomial over image of R
references.context: Commutative algebra: one-variable monic polynomial T^n+a_{n−1}T^{n−1}+…+a_0 with coefficients in the image of R in S; leading coefficient 1 and positive degree.
references.reason: Monic polynomial is a reusable ring-algebra condition; integrality needs existence of such an annihilating polynomial.
references.matching_note: Preserve ring map coefficient-image context; don't assume minimum polynomial or irreducible.

references.context: Commutative algebra: polynomial evaluation at s∈S with f(s)=0_S, for a polynomial over the image of a ring map R→S; no division or field structure is required.
references.reason: Polynomial evaluation and roots in rings are prerequisite notions distinct from integrality's monicity requirement.
references.matching_note: Do not conflate roots in a field extension with arbitrary commutative ring evaluation.

references.disposition: This is existential and imposes neither minimality nor uniqueness of the polynomial.
